name: Arad City Hall (Administrative Palace)
hint: A tower with a Swiss clock watches over the boulevard, a short walk north.
description:
The Administrative Palace at 75 Bulevardul Revoluției houses both the city hall of Arad and the prefecture of Arad County. Its tower is reminiscent of Flemish town halls, and the ornamentation draws on the Flemish Renaissance.

Arad’s town hall originally stood in Avram Iancu Square from the 17th century. As the city grew and its centre shifted, the council decided to build a new one closer to the new core. The Budapest architect Ödön Lechner produced a design, but financial problems made it impossible to build, so Ferenc Pekár modified the blueprints and cut some of the elements.

The palace was built between 1872 and 1876 and inaugurated in 1877. The clock was brought from Switzerland in the year of the inauguration and still works today. The stained glass, painted by the Arad artist Sever Frențiu, depicts the seasons.
